results.summary: This project is a reconfigurable logic circuit built from identical rotatable tiles, arranged as a 1x2 tile design. It is a minor modification of ROTFPGA v2a that simulates latches using flip-flops and combines some inputs to make room for two extra inputs, serving as a control group for latch testing on IHP. The design includes scan chain input and output pins plus configuration and loop-breaker controls, and its test suite replaces each original clock tick with 50 latch clocks, a latch-and-flip-flop clock, and 50 more latch clocks. A silicon test report from the author states it works as expected, with no external hardware required.

The design is simple and demonstrates basic counting and display. It is implemented in Verilog and targets the Tiny Tapeout platform.
results.summary: This project is a demoscene competition entry that implements a limited-precision ray tracer in two Tiny Tapeout tiles, embracing rounding errors as its primary feature. The RTL was written in HardCaml, which emits Verilog that is committed to the source tree. It renders 640x480 at 60 Hz with the eye Z coordinate animated between 3.5 and 4.5 over 256 frames, and outputs VGA on uo[0-7] plus a simple hsync/vsync audio mix on uio[7]. Setting ui[0] to 0 runs the default demo and setting it to 1 shows a color-bar test image, with an external 25.25 MHz clock required.
